text.p: Austrian cartonboard maker Mayr-Melnhof on Wednesday posted a 62.8 percent rise in 1996 pre-tax profit to 700 million schillings.
The company said it would pay a bonus dividend of 17 schillings after it paid no dividend last year.
Mayr-Melnhof said its net income exluding minority interests provisionally rose 32.3 percent in 1996 to 442 million schillings, while group turnover fell 14.3 percent to 10.5 billion schillings.

"The decrease was partly due to lower cartonboard and waste paper prices, but also because of a higher proportion of internal sales, resulting from steps to increase the level of integration between divisions," a statement said.
The price development together with higher capacity utilisation resulted in improved margins in the cartonboard division. Margins in the waste paper division suffered, the firm said.
The company said it expected "a continual satisfactory development of result" in the first quarter of 1997 and noted it would continue its expansion strategy.
